explain.say: Why is Earth cosy enough for you to live on, while the Moon, just as far from the Sun, freezes at night? The answer is a blanket of gases. Look at the board. It starts with sunlight streaming through the air.

explain.say: Some escapes to space, but look here. Greenhouse gases, like carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour, absorb the infrared and send some back down. That keeps Earth about 33 °C warmer. This is the greenhouse effect. Do you think it is good or bad?

explain.say: Both! Without it, Earth would freeze. But look at the graph. Burning coal, oil and gas has pushed carbon dioxide from about 315 parts per million in 1958 to about 424 in 2024. A thicker blanket traps more heat. What do you think that does to the temperature?

It warms up! Great thinking. Look at the carbon cycle: plants take carbon dioxide in, and living things breathe it out, in balance. Burning fuels adds extra, fast. Wow: you can help, because cycling, planting trees and saving energy all cut carbon dioxide.

stages.ask: How do humans add carbon dioxide?

faq.a: Greenhouse gases in the air absorb infrared heat given off by Earth and send some back down. This keeps Earth much warmer than it would otherwise be.
The main ones are water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane. Nitrous oxide and some man-made gases also trap heat.
asks: Is carbon dioxide a greenhouse gas?

faq.a: Infrared is invisible radiation that carries heat. You feel it as warmth from the Sun, a fire or a warm stove.

faq.q: How do humans add carbon dioxide?
faq.a: Mainly by burning fossil fuels, coal, oil and gas, for electricity, transport and industry, and by cutting down forests that would take carbon dioxide in.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life. The problem is the extra effect from human emissions, which is warming the climate.
asks: Why is global warming a problem?

facts: Carbon dioxide measured at Mauna Loa, Hawaii, rose from about 315 parts per million in 1958 to about 424 parts per million in 2024.
Without the natural greenhouse effect, Earth's average surface temperature would be about −18 °C instead of about 15 °C.
